translations.idiomatic: Works reach the report of completion, the Way attains the tribute visit—towering, vast—the people cannot find words to praise it.

sentences.zh: 又使莊作《舞馬歌》，令樂府歌之。

translations.literal: He also had Zhuang compose "Song of the Dancing Horses" and ordered the Music Bureau to sing it.
translations.idiomatic: He also had Zhuang compose the "Song of the Dancing Horses" and ordered the Music Bureau to sing it.

sentences.zh: 五年，又為侍中，領前軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he again became Palace Attendant and Colonel of the Forward Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he again became palace attendant and colonel of the forward army.

sentences.zh: 於時世祖出行，夜還，敕開門。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Shizu went out; returning at night, he ordered the gate opened.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Shizu went out; returning at night, he ordered the gate opened.

sentences.zh: 莊居守，以棨信或虛，執不奉旨，須墨詔乃開。

translations.literal: Zhuang was holding the fort; because the tally-seal message might be false, he firmly refused the order and required an ink edict before opening.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang was holding the fort; because the tally-seal message might be forged, he firmly refused the order and required a written edict in ink before opening.

sentences.zh: 上後因酒宴從容曰：「卿欲效郅君章邪？」

translations.literal: Later at a wine banquet the Emperor said casually: "Do you wish to emulate Zhi Junzhang?"
translations.idiomatic: Later at a wine banquet the emperor said casually, "Do you wish to emulate Zhi Junzhang?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣聞蒐巡有度，郊祀有節，盤於遊田，著之前誡。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant has heard that autumn hunts and patrols have their limits, suburban sacrifices have their seasons, and delight in the hunting park is recorded in prior admonitions.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I have heard that autumn hunts and patrols have their limits, suburban sacrifices have their seasons, and delight in the hunting park is recorded in prior admonitions.

sentences.zh: 陛下今蒙犯塵露，晨往宵歸，容恐不逞之徒，妄生矯詐。

translations.literal: Your Majesty now suffers exposure to dust and dew, going out in the morning and returning at night—I fear lest unscrupulous men may falsely produce deceitful pretenses.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty now braves wind and weather, setting out at dawn and returning at night—I fear that unscrupulous men may seize the moment to forge false orders.

sentences.zh: 臣是以伏須神筆，乃敢開門耳。」

translations.literal: Your servant therefore bows awaiting the divine brush before daring to open the gate."
translations.idiomatic: That is why I must wait for your written edict in your own hand before I dare open the gate."

sentences.zh: 改領游擊將軍，又領本州大中正，晉安王子勛征虜長史、廣陵太守，加冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was changed to additionally hold the title General of Mobile Forces; he also held the grand provincial arbiter of his native province, and served as chief administrator on the campaign against barbarians for Prince Zixun of Jin'an and as administrator of Guangling, with the additional title General Who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to serve as general of mobile forces and as grand provincial arbiter of his native province, and was appointed chief administrator on Prince Zixun of Jin'an's barbarian-campaign staff and administrator of Guangling, with the additional rank of general who establishes might.

sentences.zh: 改為江夏王義恭太宰長史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was changed to serve as chief administrator to Grand Preceptor Prince Yigong of Jiangxia; his generalship remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as chief administrator to Grand Preceptor Prince Jiangxia Yigong, while retaining his rank as general.

sentences.zh: 六年，又為吏部尚書，領國子博士，坐選公車令張奇免官，事在顏師伯傳。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he again became Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and concurrently Dean of the State University; he was removed from office for the matter of selecting Palace Coach Commandant Zhang Qi—the affair is in the biography of Yan Shibo.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he again became minister of personnel and concurrently dean of the state university; he was dismissed for his role in the appointment of palace coach commandant Zhang Qi—the affair is recorded in the biography of Yan Shibo.

sentences.zh: 時北中郎將新安王子鸞有盛寵，欲令招引才望，乃使子鸞板莊為長史，府尋進號撫軍，仍除長史、臨淮太守。

translations.literal: At that time the North Camp Commander, Prince Ziluan of Xin'an, enjoyed great favor; wishing to attract men of talent and reputation, he had Ziluan issue a board appointment of Zhuang as chief administrator; the princely establishment soon advanced in title to Pacifying Army, and Zhuang was appointed chief administrator and Administrator of Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Ziluan of Xin'an, as north camp commander, enjoyed great favor; wishing to attract men of talent and reputation, he had Ziluan appoint Zhuang chief administrator; the princely establishment was soon upgraded to pacifying army, and Zhuang was appointed chief administrator and administrator of Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 未拜，又除吳郡太守。

translations.literal: Before he took up the appointment, he was again appointed Administrator of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, he was appointed administrator of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 莊多疾，不樂去京師，復除前職。

translations.literal: Zhuang was frequently ill and did not wish to leave the capital; he was again appointed to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang was frequently ill and reluctant to leave the capital, so he was restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝即位，以為金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor Qianfei ascended the throne, Zhuang was made Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Purple Cord.
translations.idiomatic: When Deposed Emperor Qianfei ascended the throne, Zhuang was made grand master with the golden seal and purple cord.

sentences.zh: 初，世祖寵姬殷貴妃薨，莊為誄云：「贊軌堯門。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Xiaowu's favored consort Lady Yin died, Zhuang composed an elegy saying: "Praising the track of the Gate of Yao."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Xiaowu's favored consort Lady Yin died, Zhuang composed an elegy that read, "In praise of the path through the Gate of Yao.

sentences.zh: 引漢昭帝母趙婕妤堯母門事，廢帝在東宮，銜之。

translations.literal: He cited the affair of Emperor Zhao of Han's mother, Consort Zhao Jieyu, and the Gate of Yao's Mother; while still in the Eastern Palace, the Deposed Emperor harbored resentment against Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He cited the affair of Emperor Zhao of Han's mother, Consort Zhao Jieyu, and the Gate of Yao's Mother; the deposed emperor, while still heir apparent in the Eastern Palace, had nursed a grudge against Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 至是遣人詰責莊曰：「卿昔作殷貴妃誄，頗知有東宮不？」

translations.literal: At this time he sent someone to reproach Zhuang, saying: "You once composed the eulogy for Consort Yin of Yin—did you know there was an Eastern Palace?"
translations.idiomatic: At this point he sent someone to rebuke Zhuang, saying, "You once wrote the eulogy for Consort Yin of Yin—surely you knew there was an Eastern Palace?"

sentences.zh: 將誅之。

translations.literal: He was about to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to have him executed.

sentences.zh: 或說帝曰：「死是人之所同，政復一往之苦，不足為深困。

translations.literal: Someone said to the emperor: "Death is common to all; even a single passage of suffering is not enough to cause deep distress.
translations.idiomatic: Someone advised the emperor: "Death comes to everyone alike; even one round of hardship is not enough to cause real torment.

sentences.zh: 莊少長富貴，今且繫之尚方，使知天下苦劇，然後殺之未晚也。」

translations.literal: Zhuang has known wealth and honor from youth; for now imprison him in the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories, let him know the world's bitterness and hardship, and then kill him—it will not be too late."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang has known nothing but wealth and honor since youth; for now put him in the imperial workshops and let him learn how bitter and harsh the world can be—then execute him, and it will not be too late."

sentences.zh: 帝然其言，繫於左尚方。

translations.literal: The emperor approved this advice and imprisoned Zhuang in the Left Directorate of Imperial Manufactories.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and had Zhuang imprisoned in the left directorate of imperial manufactories.

sentences.zh: 太宗定亂，得出。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu settled the turmoil, Zhuang was released.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu put down the rebellion, Zhuang was freed.

sentences.zh: 及即位，以莊為散騎常侍、光祿大夫，加金章紫綬，領尋陽王師。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, he appointed Zhuang attendant cavalry regular attendant and grand master for splendid happiness, with the golden seal and purple cord, and supervisor to Prince Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne, he made Zhuang attendant cavalry regular attendant and grand master for splendid happiness, granted him the golden seal and purple cord, and appointed him supervisor to Prince Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 頃之，轉中書令，常侍、王師如故。

translations.literal: Shortly after, he was transferred to director of the Secretariat; his posts as regular attendant and prince's supervisor remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was moved to director of the secretariat, while retaining his posts as regular attendant and prince's supervisor.

sentences.zh: 尋加金紫光祿大夫，給親信二十人，本官並如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the additional title grand master with the golden seal and purple cord, with twenty trusted attendants; his original offices all remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was further promoted to grand master with the golden seal and purple cord and given twenty personal attendants; his existing offices were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年，卒，時年四十六，追贈右光祿大夫，常侍如故，諡曰憲子。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taishi he died, aged forty-six; posthumously awarded right grand master for splendid happiness, regular attendant as before; posthumous title Filial Son.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taishi he died at forty-six; he was posthumously made right grand master for splendid happiness with his rank as regular attendant unchanged, and given the posthumous title Filial Son.

sentences.zh: 所著文章四百餘首，行於世。

translations.literal: His writings numbered more than four hundred pieces and circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He left more than four hundred written works, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 長子颺，晉平太守。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yang was administrator of Jinping.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yang served as administrator of Jinping.

sentences.zh: 女為順帝皇后，追贈金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His daughter became empress to Emperor Shun; Zhuang was posthumously awarded grand master with the golden seal and purple cord.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter became Empress to Emperor Shun, and Zhuang was posthumously granted the rank of grand master with the golden seal and purple cord.

sentences.zh: 景文出繼智，幼為從叔球所知。

translations.literal: Jingwen was born to the lineage of Zhi; in youth he was appreciated by his father's younger cousin Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen was born into the branch descended from Zhi; as a youth he won the regard of his father's younger cousin Qiu.

sentences.zh: 美風姿，好言理，少與陳郡謝莊齊名。

translations.literal: Handsome in bearing, fond of discourse on principle; in youth he enjoyed equal fame with Xie Zhuang of Chen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Graceful in appearance and fond of reasoned discourse, in his youth he was as celebrated as Xie Zhuang of Chen commandery.

sentences.zh: 太祖甚相欽重，故為太宗娶景文妹，而以景文名與太宗同。

translations.literal: Emperor Wendi held him in great esteem, therefore had Taizong marry Jingwen's younger sister, and gave Jingwen a personal name identical to Taizong's.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wendi thought highly of him, so he had Taizong marry Jingwen's younger sister and gave Jingwen the same personal name as Taizong.

sentences.zh: 高祖第五女新安公主先適太原王景深，離絕，當以適景文，固辭以疾，故不成婚。

translations.literal: Great-Ancestor's fifth daughter, Princess Xin'an, had first been married to Wang Jingshen of Taiyuan; after separation she was to marry Jingwen, but he firmly declined on grounds of illness, so the marriage did not take place.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu's fifth daughter, Princess Xin'an, had first been married to Wang Jingshen of Taiyuan; after the marriage ended she was to be matched with Jingwen, but he firmly pleaded illness and declined, so the marriage never took place.

sentences.zh: 起家太子太傅主簿，轉太子舍人，襲爵建陵子。

translations.literal: He began his career as recorder to the grand tutor of the heir apparent, then became attendant to the heir apparent, and inherited the title Marquis of Jianling.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as recorder to the grand tutor of the heir apparent, then became an attendant to the heir apparent and inherited the title marquis of Jianling.

sentences.zh: 出為江夏王義恭、始興王濬征北、後軍二府主簿，武陵王文學，世祖撫軍記室參軍，南廣平太守，轉諮議參軍，仍度安北、鎮軍府，出為宣城太守。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as recorder to Prince Yigong of Jiangxia and Prince Jun of Shixing in their northern-campaign and rear-army establishments, literary aide to Prince Wen of Wuling, recording secretary on Emperor Xiaowu's pacifying-army staff, administrator of Nan Guangping, transferred to advisory aide, then served in the pacifying-north and pacifying-army establishments, and went out as administrator of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He served as recorder in the northern-campaign and rear-army staffs of Prince Jiangxia Yigong and Prince Shixing Jun, as literary aide to Prince Wuling Wen, as recording secretary on Emperor Xiaowu's pacifying-army staff, and as administrator of Nan Guangping; he was then made advisory aide, served in the pacifying-north and pacifying-army establishments, and was appointed administrator of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 元兇弑立，以為黃門侍郎，未及就，世祖入討，景文遣間使歸款。

translations.literal: When the usurper seized the throne, Jingwen was appointed palace gate gentleman, but before he could take up the post Emperor Xiaowu marched to punish the usurper; Jingwen sent a secret messenger to declare his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: When the usurper took power, Jingwen was named a palace gate gentleman, but before he could assume the post Emperor Xiaowu raised forces against the usurper, and Jingwen sent a secret envoy to pledge allegiance.

sentences.zh: 以父在都邑，不獲致身，及事平，頗見嫌責，猶以舊恩，除南平王鑠司空長史，不拜。

translations.literal: Because his father was in the capital he could not throw himself into the struggle; after order was restored he met with considerable suspicion and blame, yet out of old favor he was appointed chief administrator to Prince Shao of Nanping as minister of works—he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father remained in the capital he could not commit himself bodily to the cause; after the rebellion was crushed he drew considerable suspicion and reproach, yet thanks to past grace he was appointed chief administrator to Prince Nanping Shao on the minister of works' staff—he declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 出為東陽太守，入為御史中丞，秘書監，領越騎校尉，不拜，遷司徒左長史。

translations.literal: He went out as administrator of Dongyang, entered as director of the censorate and supervisor of the secretariat and concurrently commander of the rapid-as-steeds guard—he did not accept—and was transferred to left chief administrator of the minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as administrator of Dongyang, recalled as director of the censorate and supervisor of the secretariat with concurrent command of the rapid-as-steeds guard—declined—and then moved to left chief administrator under the minister of works.

sentences.zh: 上以散騎常侍舊與侍中俱掌獻替，欲高其選，以景文及會稽孔覬俱南北之望，並以補之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because attendant cavalry regular attendants had traditionally shared with attendants-in-ordinary the duty of offering remonstrance and replacement, wished to raise the standard of selection; as Jingwen and Kong Xi of Kuaiji were both men of north-south renown, both were appointed to fill the posts.
translations.idiomatic: Because attendant cavalry regular attendants had long shared with attendants-in-ordinary the duty of remonstrance and counsel, the emperor wished to elevate the quality of the appointment; Jingwen and Kong Xi of Kuaiji, both men of standing throughout north and south, were appointed to the posts.

sentences.zh: 尋復為左長史。

translations.literal: Before long he again became left chief administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again made left chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 坐姊墓開不臨赴，免官。

translations.literal: He was removed from office because when his elder sister's tomb was opened he did not attend in person.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed because he failed to attend in person when his elder sister's tomb was opened.

sentences.zh: 大明二年，復為秘書監，太子右衛率，侍中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming he again became supervisor of the secretariat, right commandant guarding the heir apparent, and attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daming he was again appointed supervisor of the secretariat, right commandant guarding the heir apparent, and attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 五年，出為安陸王子綏冠軍長史、輔國將軍、江夏內史，行郢州事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he went out as chief administrator on Prince Zisui of Anlu's staff as general who establishes might, general who assists the state, and interior minister of Jiangxia, acting for the affairs of Ying province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was sent out as chief administrator to Prince Anlu Zisui with the ranks of general who establishes might and general who assists the state, and as interior minister of Jiangxia, acting governor of Ying province.

sentences.zh: 又徵為侍中，領射聲校尉，右衛將軍，加給事中，太子中庶子，右衛如故。

translations.literal: He was again summoned as attendant-in-ordinary, concurrently commander of the sound-shooting guard, right guard general, with the additional title giver of affairs, middle aide to the heir apparent, right guard as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as attendant-in-ordinary, concurrently commander of the sound-shooting guard and right guard general, with the additional titles giver of affairs and middle aide to the heir apparent, retaining his post as right guard general.

sentences.zh: 坐與奉朝請毛法因蒱戲，得錢百二十萬，白衣領職。

translations.literal: He was punished for gambling at bo with attendant-at-court Mao Fa and winning one million two hundred thousand in cash, and served his office in plain clothes.
translations.idiomatic: He was penalized for gambling at bo with attendant-at-court Mao Fa and winning one million two hundred thousand cash, and continued in office wearing plain clothes.

sentences.zh: 尋復為侍中，領中庶子，未拜。

translations.literal: Before long he again became attendant-in-ordinary and concurrently middle aide to the heir apparent, but did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again made attendant-in-ordinary and middle aide to the heir apparent, but did not take up the latter post.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝嗣位，徙秘書監，侍中如故。

translations.literal: When Deposed Emperor Qianfei succeeded to the throne, Jingwen was transferred to supervisor of the secretariat, attendant-in-ordinary as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Deposed Emperor Qianfei ascended the throne, Jingwen was moved to supervisor of the secretariat while retaining his rank as attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 以父老自解，出為江夏王義恭太宰長史，輔國將軍、南平太守。

translations.literal: He resigned on grounds of his father's age, went out as chief administrator to Grand Preceptor Prince Yigong of Jiangxia, general who assists the state, and administrator of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: Citing his father's advanced age, he resigned and was sent out as chief administrator to Grand Preceptor Prince Jiangxia Yigong, with the ranks of general who assists the state and administrator of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 永光初，為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongguang he became Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Yongguang he was appointed minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 景和元年，遷右僕射。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jinghe he was transferred to right vice director of the imperial secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jinghe he was promoted to right vice director of the imperial secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太宗翦除暴主，又平四方，欲引朝望以佐大業，乃下詔曰：「夫良圖宣國，賞崇彝命；

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu suppressed the tyrannical ruler and also pacified the four quarters; wishing to draw men of court reputation to assist the great enterprise, he issued an edict saying: "A fine design sustains the state, and rewards should honor ordained merit;
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaowu had removed the tyrannical ruler and pacified the realm, he sought to enlist men of standing at court to help consolidate his rule and issued an edict: "Sound plans sustain the state, and rewards should honor merit ordained by tradition;

sentences.zh: 殊績顯朝，策勤王府。

translations.literal: exceptional achievement shines in court, and stratagems should record service to the princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: outstanding achievement should shine at court, and stratagems should record service rendered to the imperial house.

sentences.zh: 安南將軍、江州刺史景文，風度淹粹，理懷清暢，體兼望實，誠備夷岨。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Jiang Province Jingwen—his bearing is deep and pure, his reasoning clear and fluent, his person combining reputation and substance, his loyalty embracing both the level and the rugged.
translations.idiomatic: General who pacifies the south and inspector of Jiang province Jingwen—his bearing is refined and pure, his mind clear and penetrating, his person equal to his reputation, his loyalty steadfast in easy times and hard.

sentences.zh: 寶曆方啟，密贊義機，妖徒干紀，預毗廟略。

translations.literal: As the precious succession was about to open, he secretly assisted the righteous design; when rebellious factions violated discipline, he took part in planning at the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: As the imperial succession was about to begin, he secretly supported the righteous coup; when rebels violated order, he shared in the temple councils of war.

sentences.zh: 宜登茅社，永傳厥祚。

translations.literal: He should be invested with a fief of soil and his line perpetually transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: He should receive a territorial fief and transmit his line forever.

sentences.zh: 朕澄氛寧樞，實資多士，疏爵疇庸，實膺徽烈。

translations.literal: I have clarified the mists and secured the pivot of rule, truly relying on many scholars; in granting ranks to reward merit, I have indeed received their splendid service.
translations.idiomatic: I have cleared the air at the center of power and truly depend on many able men; in ennobling merit I have indeed received their outstanding service.

sentences.zh: 尚書右僕射、領衛尉興宗，識懷詳正，思局通敏。

translations.literal: Right vice director of the imperial secretariat and concurrently commandant of the guard Xingzong—his understanding and intent are detailed and upright, his thought comprehensive and keen.
translations.idiomatic: Right vice director of the imperial secretariat and concurrent commandant of the guard Xingzong—his mind is thorough and upright, his judgment broad and sharp.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書、領太子左衛率淵，器情閑茂，風業韶遠。

translations.literal: Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and concurrently left commandant guarding the heir apparent Yuan—his talent and disposition are easy and flourishing, his style and achievement elegant and far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of personnel and concurrent left commandant guarding the heir apparent Yuan—his talent is balanced and flourishing, his conduct refined and far-sighted.

sentences.zh: 並謀參軍政，績亮時艱，拓宇開邑，實允勳典。

translations.literal: Together they plotted in military and civil affairs, their achievement bright in the time of hardship; in expanding territory and opening settlements they truly fulfilled the canon of merit.
translations.idiomatic: Together they advised on civil and military affairs and shone in those difficult years; in expanding territory and establishing settlements they truly fulfilled the standards of rewarded service.

sentences.zh: 景文可封江安縣侯，食邑八百戶，興宗可始昌縣伯，淵可南城縣伯，食邑五百戶。」

translations.literal: Jingwen may be enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiang'an with eight hundred households; Xingzong may be enfeoffed as Baron of Shichang; Yuan may be enfeoffed as Baron of Nancheng, each with five hundred households."
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen shall be enfeoffed as marquis of Jiang'an with eight hundred households; Xingzong as baron of Shichang; Yuan as baron of Nancheng—each with five hundred households."

sentences.zh: 景文固讓，不許，乃受五百戶。

translations.literal: Jingwen firmly declined but was not permitted, and therefore accepted five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen repeatedly declined but was overruled, and in the end accepted a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 進號鎮南將軍，尋給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the South; soon he was granted one set of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general who pacifies the south and soon granted a full set of martial music.

sentences.zh: 後以江州當徙鎮南昌，領豫章太守，餘如故；

translations.literal: Later, because Jiang province was to be moved to garrison Nanchang, he concurrently held the post of administrator of Yuzhang; the rest remained as before;
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Jiang province was slated to move its seat to Nanchang, he was also made administrator of Yuzhang, with his other posts unchanged;

sentences.zh: 州不果遷。

translations.literal: the provincial move did not in the end take place.
translations.idiomatic: the provincial relocation never took place.

sentences.zh: 頃之，徵為尚書左僕射，領吏部，揚州刺史，加太子詹事，常侍如故。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned as left vice director of the imperial secretariat, concurrently minister of personnel and inspector of Yang province, with the additional post of grand tutor to the heir apparent, regular attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled as left vice director of the imperial secretariat, concurrently minister of personnel and inspector of Yang province, with the additional title grand tutor to the heir apparent, retaining his rank as regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 不願還朝，求為湘州刺史，不許。

translations.literal: Unwilling to return to court, he requested to be inspector of Xiang province but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Reluctant to return to the capital, he asked to be made inspector of Xiang province, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 時又謂景文在江州，不能潔己。

translations.literal: At the time it was also said that while Jingwen was in Jiang province he could not keep himself pure.
translations.idiomatic: At the time people also claimed that Jingwen, while serving in Jiang province, had failed to keep his conduct clean.

sentences.zh: 景文與上幸臣王道龍書曰：「吾雖寡於行己，庶不負心，既愧殊效，誓不上欺明主。

translations.literal: Jingwen wrote to the emperor's favorite Wang Daolong, saying: "Although I am poor in conduct, I trust I have not betrayed my heart; having fallen short of special achievement, I swear I would not deceive my enlightened lord above.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen wrote to the emperor's favorite Wang Daolong: "Though I am weak in personal conduct, I believe I have not been false in heart; having failed to perform any outstanding service, I would never deceive my sovereign.

sentences.zh: 竊聞有為其貝錦者，云營生乃至巨萬，素無此能，一旦忽致異術，必非平理。

translations.literal: I have heard that someone is weaving brocaded slander against me, saying my business dealings reach huge sums—yet I have never had such ability; if such strange skill suddenly appeared, it cannot be reasonable.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that someone is fabricating charges against me, claiming my business dealings run to enormous sums—yet I have never had such skill; if such sudden wealth appeared, it could not be honest.

sentences.zh: 唯乞平心精檢，若此言不虛，便宜肆諸市朝，以正風俗。

translations.literal: I only beg that you examine this with a level mind; if these words are not empty, I should gladly be exposed in the marketplace to correct public morals.
translations.idiomatic: I ask only that you investigate this fairly; if the accusation is true, I deserve to be displayed in the public square to set the moral tone.

sentences.zh: 脫其妄作，當賜思罔昧之由。

translations.literal: If it is falsely made up, I should be told the reason for such reckless invention.
translations.idiomatic: If it is a fabrication, I should be told why such slander was invented.

sentences.zh: 吾逾忝轉深，足以致謗，念此驚懼，何能自測。

translations.literal: My undeserved honors grow ever deeper, enough to invite slander; thinking of this fills me with alarm—how can I measure myself?
translations.idiomatic: My undeserved promotions grow ever weightier, enough to draw calumny; the thought fills me with dread, and I cannot judge myself.

sentences.zh: 區區所懷，不願望風容貸。

translations.literal: What I feel in my heart is that I do not wish to be spared out of favor.
translations.idiomatic: What I feel in my heart is that I do not ask to be excused out of personal favor.

sentences.zh: 吾自了不作偷，猶如不作賊。

translations.literal: I myself know I would no more steal than I would become a thief.
translations.idiomatic: I know myself: I am no more capable of theft than I am of becoming a robber.

sentences.zh: 故以密白，想為申啟。」

translations.literal: Therefore I report this in confidence, hoping you will relay it and speak for me."
translations.idiomatic: So I write to you in confidence, hoping you will raise this on my behalf."

sentences.zh: 景文屢辭內授，上手詔譬之曰：「尚書左僕射，卿已經此任，東宮詹事，用人雖美，職次正可比中書令耳。

translations.literal: Jingwen repeatedly declined appointments within the capital; the emperor sent a personal edict to reason with him, saying: "Left vice director of the imperial secretariat—you have already held this office; grand tutor to the heir apparent, though the man appointed is fine, in rank of duty it can only be compared to director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen repeatedly declined posts at court; the emperor wrote to persuade him: "As left vice director of the imperial secretariat you have already served in that capacity; as grand tutor to the heir apparent the appointee may be worthy, but in rank the duty is truly comparable only to director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 庶姓作揚州，徐干木、王休元、殷鐵並處之不辭。

translations.literal: Commoners have held Yang province—Xu Ganmu, Wang Xiuyuan, and Yin Tie all took the post without declining.
translations.idiomatic: Men of non-imperial surname have held Yang province—Xu Ganmu, Wang Xiuyuan, and Yin Tie all accepted without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 卿清令才望，何愧休元；

translations.literal: Your pure talent and reputation—what shame is there compared with Xiuyuan;
translations.idiomatic: With your refined talent and reputation, what have you to fear compared with Xiuyuan;

sentences.zh: 毗贊中興，豈謝干木；

translations.literal: in assisting the restoration, how would you fall short of Ganmu;
translations.idiomatic: in aiding the restoration, how would you rank below Ganmu;

sentences.zh: 綢繆相與，何後殷鐵邪？

translations.literal: in intimate cooperation, how are you behind Yin Tie?
translations.idiomatic: in close cooperation with the throne, how are you inferior to Yin Tie?

sentences.zh: 司徒以宰相不應帶神州，遠遵先旨，京口鄉基義重，密邇畿內，又不得不用驃騎，陝西任要，由來用宗室。

translations.literal: The minister of works held that a chief minister should not also hold the capital province; far obeying the former intent, Jingkou as the ancestral seat of the house carries heavy meaning and lies close within the inner precincts, so the post of general of swift cavalry cannot but be used; the strategic post in Shaanxi has from old been filled by imperial clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: The minister of works argued that a chief minister should not also govern the capital province; honoring the earlier policy, Jingkou as the dynasty's ancestral base is weighty and lies near the inner capital, so the post of general of swift cavalry must be filled; the key post in the west has traditionally gone to members of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 驃騎既去，巴陵理應居之，中流雖曰閑地，控帶三江，通接荊、郢，經塗之要，由來有重鎮。

translations.literal: Once the general of swift cavalry departs, Baling ought rightly to occupy it; the middle Yangzi, though called a quiet region, controls the three Jiang rivers and connects Jing and Ying—on the main routes it has always been a place of heavy garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Once the general of swift cavalry leaves, Baling should rightly take the post; the middle Yangzi, though called a quiet region, commands the three Jiang rivers and links Jing and Ying—on the great routes it has always required strong garrisons.

sentences.zh: 如此，則揚州自成闕刺史，卿若有辭，更不知誰應處之。

translations.literal: Thus Yang province by itself lacks a candidate for inspector; if you decline, I no longer know who should take it.
translations.idiomatic: In that case Yang province would have no one else to appoint inspector; if you refuse, I truly do not know who should hold it.

sentences.zh: 此選大備，與公卿疇懷，非聊爾也。」

translations.literal: This selection is fully considered, aligned with the thoughts of the lords and ministers—it is not a casual matter."
translations.idiomatic: This appointment has been fully weighed and matches what the ministers feel—it is no light matter."

sentences.zh: 固辭詹事領選，徙為中書令，常侍、僕射、揚州如故。

translations.literal: He firmly declined the grand tutorship and concurrent personnel selection, and was transferred to director of the Secretariat, regular attendant, vice director, and Yang inspector as before.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined the grand tutorship and concurrent control of appointments and was moved to director of the secretariat, retaining his posts as regular attendant, vice director, and inspector of Yang province.

sentences.zh: 又進中書監，領太子太傅，常侍、揚州如故。

translations.literal: He was further promoted to supervisor of the Secretariat and concurrently grand tutor to the heir apparent, regular attendant and Yang inspector as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to supervisor of the secretariat and grand tutor to the heir apparent, while remaining regular attendant and inspector of Yang province.

sentences.zh: 景文固辭太傅，上遣新除尚書右僕射褚淵宣旨，以古來比例六事詰難之，不得已，乃受拜。

translations.literal: Jingwen firmly declined the grand tutorship; the emperor sent the newly appointed right vice director of the imperial secretariat Chu Yuan to announce the imperial will, using six historical parallels to press the point; unable to refuse further, he at last accepted the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen repeatedly declined the grand tutorship; the emperor sent the newly appointed right vice director Chu Yuan to deliver the imperial message, citing six historical precedents to argue him into acceptance; with no choice left, he finally took the post.

sentences.zh: 時太子及諸皇子並小，上稍為身後之計，諸將帥吳喜、壽寂之之徒，慮其不能奉幼主，並殺之；

translations.literal: At that time the heir apparent and all the princes were still young; the emperor gradually made plans for after his death; among the generals Wu Xi and Shou Jizhi and their like, fearing they would not loyally serve a young ruler, he had them all killed;
translations.idiomatic: At that time the heir apparent and the princes were all still young; the emperor began planning for the time after his death; fearing that generals such as Wu Xi and Shou Jizhi would not faithfully serve a child emperor, he had them all executed;

sentences.zh: 而景文外戚貴盛，張永累經軍旅，又疑其將來難信，乃自為謠言曰：「一士不可親，弓長射殺人。」

translations.literal: yet Jingwen as an eminent maternal relative and Zhang Yong, who had repeatedly campaigned, were also suspected as men who might not be trusted in the future; he therefore himself spread a rhyme saying: "One scholar must not be trusted—the bow long shoots men dead."
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen, as a powerful maternal relative, and Zhang Yong, a veteran of many campaigns, were also feared as men who might not prove loyal later; the emperor therefore spread a rhyme himself: "One scholar must not be trusted—bow long shoots a man dead."

sentences.zh: 一士，王字；

translations.literal: "One scholar" is the character Wang;
translations.idiomatic: "One scholar" stands for the character Wang;"

sentences.zh: 弓長，張字也。

translations.literal: "bow long" is the character Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: "bow long" stands for the character Zhang."

sentences.zh: 景文彌懼，乃自陳求解揚州，曰：

translations.literal: Jingwen grew ever more fearful and therefore submitted a memorial asking to be relieved of Yang province, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen grew ever more afraid and memorialized asking to be released from Yang province, stating:

sentences.zh: 臣凡猥下劣，方圜無筭，特逢聖私，頻叨不次，乘非其任，理宜覆折。

translations.literal: Your servant is altogether base and inferior, without measure in square or round; I have specially met with sacred favor and repeatedly received unorthodox promotions, occupying a post not my due—by right I should be overturned and broken.
translations.idiomatic: I am altogether base and unworthy, without judgment in matters of principle; I have been singled out for imperial favor and repeatedly promoted out of turn, holding a post beyond my capacity—for which I ought rightly to be cast down.

sentences.zh: 雖加恭謹，無補橫至，夙夜燋戰，無地容處。

translations.literal: Though I add reverence and caution, it does not repair what has come upon me horizontally; day and night I burn with dread, with no place to contain myself.
translations.idiomatic: However reverent and cautious I become, it cannot undo what has befallen me; day and night I burn with fear and have nowhere to hide.

sentences.zh: 六月中，得臣外甥女殷恆妻蔡疏，欲令其兒啟聞乞祿，求臣署入，云凡外人通啟，先經臣署。

translations.literal: In the sixth month I received a memorial from Lady Cai, wife of Yin Heng, my niece by marriage, wishing to have her son submit a petition begging for salary and asking me to sign the entry, saying that all outside petitions must first pass through my office.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month I received a petition from Lady Cai, wife of my niece's husband Yin Heng, asking that her son submit a request for salary with my signature on the cover, on the ground that all outside petitions must first go through me.

sentences.zh: 於時驚怖，即欲封疏上呈；

translations.literal: At the time I was alarmed and immediately wished to seal the memorial and send it up;
translations.idiomatic: At the time I was terrified and at once wanted to seal the document and send it upward;

sentences.zh: 更思此家落漠，庶非通謗，且廣聽察，幸無復所聞。

translations.literal: on further thought this family was obscure and presumably not engaged in slander, and I broadened my listening and investigation—fortunately nothing more was heard.
translations.idiomatic: on reflection that family was obscure and probably not plotting slander, I widened my inquiries and fortunately heard nothing more.

sentences.zh: 比日忽得兗州都送迎西曹解季遜板云是臣屬，既不識此人，即問郗顒，方知虛託。

translations.literal: Recently, on the seventeenth day, I received a board from Yan province's west bureau escort officer Xie Jiyun saying he was my subordinate; not knowing the man, I asked Xi Yan and then learned it was a false claim.
translations.idiomatic: Then on the seventeenth I received a dispatch from Xie Jiyun of Yan province's west bureau escort, claiming to be my subordinate; not knowing him, I questioned Xi Yan and learned the claim was fabricated.

sentences.zh: 比十七日晚，得征南參軍事謝儼口信，云臣使人略奪其婢。

translations.literal: On the evening of the seventeenth I received an oral message from Xie Yan, staff officer on the campaign against the south, saying my agent had roughly seized his maid.
translations.idiomatic: That same evening I received word from Xie Yan, staff officer on the southern campaign, that someone sent by me had forcibly taken his maidservant.

sentences.zh: 臣遣李武之問儼元由，答云「使人謬誤」。

translations.literal: I sent Li Wuzhi to ask Yan the original reason; he answered that "the messenger erred."
translations.idiomatic: I sent Li Wuzhi to ask Yan how this arose; he replied that "the messenger made a mistake."

sentences.zh: 誤之與實，雖所不知，聞此之日，唯有憂駭。

translations.literal: Whether error or fact, though I do not know, on the day I heard this I had only worry and shock.
translations.idiomatic: Whether mistake or truth I cannot say, but the day I heard it I was only alarmed and shaken.

sentences.zh: 臣之所知，便有此三變，臣所不覺，尤不可思。

translations.literal: What I know of myself already has these three changes; what I do not notice is especially unthinkable.
translations.idiomatic: Within my own knowledge there have already been these three incidents; what I do not even notice is all the more frightening.

sentences.zh: 若守爵散輩，寧當招此，誠由闇拙，非復可防。

translations.literal: If I merely kept a noble title among the idle, would I invite such things? Truly it is because I am dull and clumsy that it cannot be guarded against further.
translations.idiomatic: If I held only an empty noble rank among the idle, would such things befall me? It is truly because I am obtuse and awkward that I cannot guard against them.

sentences.zh: 自竊州任，倏已七月，無德而祿，其殃將至。

translations.literal: Since I privately assumed provincial duty it has already been seven months—salary without virtue, and calamity is about to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Since I took private charge of the province seven months have passed—emolument without merit, and disaster is near.

sentences.zh: 且傅職清峻，亢禮儲極，以臣凡走，豈可暫安。

translations.literal: Moreover the grand tutorship is pure and lofty, matching in ritual the heir's utmost station—with my altogether base running, how can I briefly rest at ease?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the grand tutorship is pure and exalted, equal in ritual standing to the heir apparent—how can someone as unworthy as I rest easy even for a moment?

sentences.zh: 荷恩懼罪，不敢執固，焦魂褫氣，憂迫失常。

translations.literal: Bearing grace yet fearing guilt, I dare not hold stubbornly; my scorched soul is stripped of breath, worry and pressure driving me from the normal.
translations.idiomatic: Loaded with favor yet fearing punishment, I dare not stand firm; my spirit is burned hollow and my breath taken away, anxiety pressing me out of my right mind.

sentences.zh: 況臣髮醜人群，病絕力效，穢朝點列，顧無與等，獨息易駭，慚懼難持。

translations.literal: Moreover, your servant's hair is ugly among the crowd, illness cuts off strength for service; stained in the court's roster, I look and find no equal—alone my breath is easily startled, shame and fear hard to sustain.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I am a sorry sight among men, my illness leaves me no strength to serve; listed among the court's ranks, I see no one my equal—left alone I startle at every breath, shame and fear I can barely bear.

sentences.zh: 伏願薄回矜愍，全臣身計，大夫之俸，足以自周，久懷欣羡，未敢干請，仰希慈宥，照臣款誠。

translations.literal: I bow and wish for slight turning of pity and compassion, to preserve your servant's personal plan—the salary of a grandee is enough for self-sufficiency; long I have cherished and admired this, not daring to importune; looking up I hope for gracious pardon, illuminating your servant's sincere plea.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to turn a little pity my way and spare my person—the stipend of a grandee would be enough to live on; I have long wished for this but never dared ask; I look up hoping for your mercy, that you may see my honest request.

sentences.zh: 上詔答曰：

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict in reply:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied by edict:

sentences.zh: 去五月中，吾病始差，未堪勞役，使卿等看選牒，署竟，請敕施行。

translations.literal: In the fifth month gone by my illness had just eased; not yet able to bear labor, I had you and the others review selection dossiers; when the signing was done, I requested the edict be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Last fifth month my illness had just improved; still unable to bear heavy work, I had you review the appointment registers, and once the signing was finished I ordered the edict implemented.

sentences.zh: 此非密事，外間不容都不聞。

translations.literal: This was not a secret matter—outside it could not be that none heard of it at all.
translations.idiomatic: This was no secret—it could not be that the outside world heard nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 然傳事好訛，由來常患。

translations.literal: Yet transmitted affairs easily err—this has always been a worry.
translations.idiomatic: Yet rumors distort events, as they always have.

sentences.zh: 殷恆妻，匹婦耳，閨閣之內，傳聞事復作一兩倍落漠，兼謂卿是親故，希卿署，不必云選事獨關卿也。

translations.literal: Yin Heng's wife is only a common woman; within women's quarters, transmitted affairs again become one or two degrees more obscure; it was also said you were a close relation and that she hoped for your signature—not necessarily that selection affairs concern you alone.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Heng's wife is only a housewife; inside the women's quarters gossip grows twice as murky; people also said you were kin and that she hoped for your signature—not that appointments depend on you alone.

sentences.zh: 恆妻雖是傳聞之僻，大都非可駭異。

translations.literal: Though Yin Heng's wife was a remote transmitted matter, on the whole it was nothing to be alarmed at.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the story about Yin Heng's wife was distant hearsay, on the whole it was hardly shocking.

sentences.zh: 且舉元薦凱，咸由疇諮，可謂唐堯不明，下干其政邪？

translations.literal: Moreover recommending the worthy and promoting the splendid—all come from consultation among peers; can one say Emperor Yao was unenlightened and that inferiors meddled in his government?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, recommending talent and advancing the able all flow from collegial consultation—can one say Emperor Yao was dim and that subordinates interfered in his rule?

sentences.zh: 悠悠好詐貴人及在事者，屬卿偶不悉耳，多是其周旋門生輩，作其屬託，貴人及在事者，永無由知。

translations.literal: Those who idly love deceit—the noble and those in office—when you happen not to know fully, mostly it is their student companions in social rounds who make false entrustments; the noble and those in office have never a way to know.
translations.idiomatic: As for busy schemers among the great and the officeholders—you simply did not know the whole story; usually it is their student hangers-on who forge entreaties in their names, and the great and the officeholders never learn of it.

sentences.zh: 非徒止於京師，乃至州郡縣中，或有詐作書疏，灼然有文跡者。

translations.literal: It does not stop at the capital alone—even in prefectures, commanderies, and counties there are sometimes forged letters and memorials with plainly visible writing.
translations.idiomatic: It is not only in the capital—even in prefectures, commanderies, and counties people sometimes forge letters and petitions with clear written traces.

sentences.zh: 諸舍人右丞輩，及親近驅使人，慮有作其名，載禁物，求停檢校，強賣猥物與官，仍求交直，或屬人求乞州郡資禮，希蠲呼召及虜發船車，並啟班下在所，有即駐錄。

translations.literal: The palace gentlemen, right assistants, and close attendants and drivers—fearing someone might use their names to carry forbidden goods, seek to halt inspection, forcibly sell base goods to officials and still demand payment, or entrust others to beg for provincial salary gifts, hope to be exempted from summons and from requisition of boats and carts—all such petitions are recorded wherever they appear and immediately detained.
translations.idiomatic: Palace gentlemen, right assistants, close servants and runners—fearing impersonation to smuggle contraband, dodge inspection, force shoddy goods on officials for cash, or beg provincial gifts and exemptions from summons and transport levies—all such petitions are logged and held wherever they turn up.

sentences.zh: 但卿貴人，不容有此啟。

translations.literal: But you are a noble—such petitions cannot be allowed for you.
translations.idiomatic: But you are a man of rank—such petitions cannot belong to you.

sentences.zh: 由來有是，何故獨驚！

translations.literal: There have always been such things—why be alarmed alone!
translations.idiomatic: Such things have always existed—why should you alone be shaken!

sentences.zh: 人居貴要，但問心若為耳。

translations.literal: When a man dwells in nobility and importance, one need only ask how his heart is.
translations.idiomatic: For a man in high and weighty station, only the state of his heart matters.

sentences.zh: 大明之世，巢、徐、二戴，位不過執戟，權亢人主；

translations.literal: In the Daming era, Chao, Xu, and the two Dai— their posts did not exceed halberd-bearer, yet their power rivaled the lord of men;
translations.idiomatic: In the Daming reign, Chao, Xu, and the two Dai held ranks no higher than halberd-bearer, yet their power equaled the emperor's;

sentences.zh: 顏師伯白衣僕射，橫行尚書中。

translations.literal: Yan Shibo as plain-clothes vice director, striding through the midst of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shibo served as vice director in plain clothes, striding through the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 令袁粲作僕射領選，而人往往不知有粲。

translations.literal: When Yuan Can was made vice director concurrently overseeing selection, people often did not even know Can existed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Can became vice director with control of appointments, many people scarcely knew he was there.

sentences.zh: 粲遷為令，居之不疑。

translations.literal: Can was transferred to director and occupied the post without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Can was moved to director and took the post as a matter of course.

sentences.zh: 今既省錄，令便居昔之錄任，置省事及榦童，竝依錄格。

translations.literal: Now that the secretariat has been reduced, the director's post occupies what was formerly the recorder's duty; setting up clerks and page boys all follows the recorder's standard.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the secretariat has been streamlined, the director holds what the recorder once did; clerks and runners are arranged by the old recorder's rules.

sentences.zh: 粲作令來，亦不異為僕射。

translations.literal: Since Can became director, it has not differed from being vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Since Can became director, the role has differed little from vice director.

sentences.zh: 人情向粲，淡淡然亦復不改常。

translations.literal: Popular feeling turned toward Can, yet calmly he also did not change his usual ways.
translations.idiomatic: Public favor leaned toward Can, yet he remained as calm and unchanged as ever.

sentences.zh: 以此居貴位要任，當有致憂兢理不？

translations.literal: Thus occupying noble rank and weighty duty—should there not be reason for worry and caution?
translations.idiomatic: If that is how one holds high rank and heavy responsibility, is there not cause for caution?

sentences.zh: 卿今雖作揚州，太子傅位雖貴，而不關朝政，可安不懼，差於粲也。

translations.literal: Though you now serve as Yang inspector, the grand tutor's post, though noble, does not touch court governance—you may rest without fear, better off than Can.
translations.idiomatic: Though you are inspector of Yang province, the grand tutorship, though honored, does not touch court policy—you may live without fear, safer than Can.

sentences.zh: 想卿虛心受榮，而不為累。

translations.literal: I think you will empty your heart to accept honor and not be burdened by it.
translations.idiomatic: I trust you will accept honor with an open heart and not be crushed by it.

sentences.zh: 貴高有危殆之懼，卑賤有溝壑之憂，張、單雙災，木雁兩失，有心於避禍，不如無心於任運。

translations.literal: The noble and high have fear of peril; the base and lowly have worry of the ditch—Zhang and Shan suffered twin disasters, the big tree and wild goose both lost; the heart that seeks to flee calamity is not as good as the heartless acceptance of fate's course.
translations.idiomatic: The lofty fear danger, the humble fear the gutter—Zhang and Shan met double disaster, tree and goose both lost; trying to dodge disaster is not as good as accepting fate without strain.

sentences.zh: 夫千仞之木，既摧於斧斤；

translations.literal: A tree of a thousand ren, once struck by axe and adze, is felled;
translations.idiomatic: A tree a thousand ren high is still cut down by axe and hatchet;

sentences.zh: 一寸之草，亦瘁於踐蹋。

translations.literal: a blade of grass one inch long also withers under trampling.
translations.idiomatic: a blade of grass an inch long withers underfoot.

sentences.zh: 高崖之脩榦，與深谷之淺條，存亡之要，巨細一揆耳。

translations.literal: The tall trunk on a high cliff and the shallow branch in a deep ravine—the crux of survival and destruction, great and small, follow one measure.
translations.idiomatic: The tall trunk on a cliff and the thin branch in a ravine—whether they live or die, great or small, obey the same law.

sentences.zh: 晉畢萬七戰皆獲，死於牖下；

translations.literal: In Jin, Bi Wan won in seven battles yet died beneath a window;
translations.idiomatic: In Jin, Bi Wan won seven battles yet died under his own roof;

sentences.zh: 蜀相費禕從容坐談，斃於刺客。

translations.literal: Shu's chancellor Fei Yi, sitting at ease in conversation, was slain by an assassin.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's chancellor Fei Yi, talking at ease, was killed by an assassin.

sentences.zh: 故甘心於履危，未必逢禍；

translations.literal: Therefore willingly treading danger does not necessarily meet calamity;
translations.idiomatic: So those who willingly walk in peril do not necessarily meet disaster;

sentences.zh: 縱意於處安，不必全福。

translations.literal: indulging the will in dwelling in safety does not necessarily preserve full blessing.
translations.idiomatic: those who indulge ease do not necessarily keep full fortune.

sentences.zh: 但貴者自惜，故每憂其身；

translations.literal: But the noble cherish themselves, therefore they always worry for their persons;
translations.idiomatic: The great cherish themselves and so always fear for their lives;

sentences.zh: 賤者自輕，故易忘其己。

translations.literal: the base despise themselves, therefore they easily forget themselves.
translations.idiomatic: the lowly despise themselves and easily forget their own worth.

sentences.zh: 然為教者，每誡貴不誡賤，言其貴滿好自恃也。

translations.literal: Yet in teaching, one always admonishes the noble and not the base, saying that the noble, full and complacent, love to rely on themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Yet teachers always warn the great, not the humble, because the privileged, swollen with pride, trust too much in themselves.

sentences.zh: 凡名位貴達，人以在懷，泰則觸人改容，不則行路嗟愕。

translations.literal: Whenever name, rank, nobility, and success are held, men keep them in mind; in prosperity they touch others to change countenance, otherwise passers on the road gasp in surprise.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever men hold fame, rank, and success, others take note; in good times they make people change face, in bad times they make strangers stare in shock.

sentences.zh: 至如賤者，否泰不足以動人，存亡不足以絓數，死於溝瀆，死於塗路者，天地之間，亦復何限，人不以係意耳。

translations.literal: As for the base, prosperity and adversity are not enough to move people, survival and destruction not enough to tie the count; those who die in ditches and on roads—between Heaven and Earth they are also beyond limit, and men do not attach their thoughts to them.
translations.idiomatic: For the humble, rise and fall hardly stir anyone, life and death hardly enter the reckoning; those who die in gutters and on roads are beyond counting under Heaven, and no one much cares.

sentences.zh: 以此而推，貴何必難處，賤何必易安。

translations.literal: Pushing from this, why must the noble be hard to dwell in, why must the base be easy to rest in?
translations.idiomatic: From this one sees that high station need not be hard to bear, nor low station easy to endure.

sentences.zh: 但人生也自應卑慎為道，行己用心，務思謹惜。

translations.literal: But human life itself should take humility and caution as the Way; in conduct and in heart one should strive to think carefully and cherish oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in life one should walk the path of humility and caution, acting and thinking with constant care for oneself.

sentences.zh: 若乃吉凶大期，正應委之理運，遭隨參差，莫不由命也。

translations.literal: As for the great term of fortune and calamity, one should indeed entrust it to principle and fate; meeting with uneven fortune is never not from mandate.
translations.idiomatic: When the great turning of fortune arrives, one should leave it to reason and fate; uneven fortune always comes by destiny.

sentences.zh: 既非聖人，不能見吉凶之先，正是依俙於理，言可行而為之耳。

translations.literal: Not being sages, we cannot see fortune and calamity beforehand—we can only rely on principle and speak of what can be done and do it.
translations.idiomatic: Not being sages, we cannot foresee fortune or disaster—we can only trust in reason and do what can be done.

sentences.zh: 得吉者是其命吉，遇不吉者是其命凶。

translations.literal: Those who obtain fortune—it is their mandate of fortune; those who meet misfortune—it is their mandate of misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: Those who meet good fortune have a fortunate fate; those who meet ill have an ill fate.

sentences.zh: 以近事論之，景和之世，晉平庶人從壽陽歸亂朝，人皆為之戰慄，而乃遇中興之運；

translations.literal: Judging from recent affairs, in the Jinghe era the commoner of Jinping followed disorder from Shouyang back to court—everyone trembled for him, yet he met the fortune of restoration;
translations.idiomatic: Take recent events: in the Jinghe era the Jinping commoner returned from Shouyang amid rebellion—everyone feared for him, yet he rode the tide of restoration;

sentences.zh: 袁顗圖避禍於襄陽，當時皆羨之，謂為陵霄駕鳳，遂與義嘉同滅。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao sought to flee calamity at Xiangyang—at the time all envied him, calling it driving the phoenix above the clouds, yet he perished together with Yijia.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao tried to escape disaster at Xiangyang—everyone envied him, saying he soared like a phoenix, yet he fell with Yijia.

sentences.zh: 駱宰見幼主，語人云：「越王長頸鳥喙，可與共憂，不可與共樂。

translations.literal: Assistant Lu, seeing the young lord, told people: "The King of Yue has a long neck and bird's beak—one can share worry with him, not share joy.
translations.idiomatic: Clerk Lu, meeting the young emperor, said to others, "The King of Yue had a long neck and a bird's beak—you can share worry with such a man, not joy.

sentences.zh: 范蠡去而全身，文種留而遇禍。

translations.literal: Fan Li left and preserved his whole person; Wen Zhong stayed and met calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Li withdrew and saved himself whole; Wen Zhong stayed and was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 今主上口頸，頗有越王之狀，我在尚書中久，不去必危。」

translations.literal: Now our lord's mouth and neck quite have the King of Yue's appearance; I have long been in the Ministry of Personnel—if I do not leave, peril is certain."
translations.idiomatic: Our lord's mouth and neck resemble the King of Yue's; I have served long in the ministry of personnel—if I do not leave, I am doomed."

sentences.zh: 遂求南江小縣。

translations.literal: He therefore requested a small county on the southern Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: So he asked for a minor post on the southern Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 諸都令史住京師者，皆遭中興之慶，人人蒙爵級；

translations.literal: All the clerks of commandery and county who resided in the capital met the celebration of restoration—every man received rank and stipend;
translations.idiomatic: The clerks of commanderies and counties who lived in the capital all shared in the joy of restoration—every man gained rank and pay;

sentences.zh: 宰值義嘉染罪，金木纏身，性命幾絕。

translations.literal: Lu, having been stained by Yijia's guilt, was bound by metal and wood, his life nearly ended.
translations.idiomatic: Lu, tainted by Yijia's crime, was shackled in metal and wood and nearly lost his life.

sentences.zh: 卿耳眼所聞見，安危在運，何可預圖邪！

translations.literal: What your ears and eyes have heard and seen—safety and peril lie in fate; how can one plan ahead!
translations.idiomatic: What you have heard and seen proves that safety and danger rest on fate—how can one plan ahead?

sentences.zh: 時上既有疾，而諸弟並已見殺，唯桂陽王休範人才本劣，不見疑，出為江州刺史。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor already had illness, and his younger brothers had all been killed; only Prince Xiufan of Guiyang, whose talent was originally inferior, was not suspected, and was sent out as inspector of Jiang province.
translations.idiomatic: By then the emperor was already ill and his younger brothers had all been killed; only Prince Guiyang Xiufan, a man of lesser ability, was not suspected and was sent out as inspector of Jiang province.

sentences.zh: 慮一旦晏駕，皇后臨朝，則景文自然成宰相，門族強盛，藉元舅之重，歲暮不為純臣。

translations.literal: Fearing that once he died the empress would hold court, Jingwen would naturally become chief minister; his clan was powerful, relying on the weight of maternal uncle to the Yuan clan—at year's end he would not remain a pure minister.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that when the emperor died the empress would rule, Jingwen would naturally become chief minister; his clan was powerful as maternal kin to the imperial house—by year's end he would no longer be a loyal subject.

sentences.zh: 泰豫元年春，上疾篤，乃遣使送藥賜景文死，手詔曰：「與卿周旋，欲全卿門戶，故有此處分。」

translations.literal: In spring of the first year of Taiyu the emperor's illness was grave; he sent an envoy with medicine to grant Jingwen death, writing by his own hand: "In our rounds together I wished to preserve your clan's gate and household—therefore this disposition."
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the first year of Taiyu the emperor's illness turned critical; he sent an envoy with poison to grant Jingwen death, writing in his own hand, "In our long association I meant to preserve your house—hence this measure."

sentences.zh: 死時年六十。

translations.literal: At death he was sixty years old.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty.

sentences.zh: 追贈車騎將軍、開府儀同三司，常侍、中書監、刺史如故，諡曰懿侯。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded general of chariots and cavalry and grand master with the same ceremonial trappings as opening a headquarters, regular attendant, supervisor of the Secretariat, and inspector as before; posthumous title Marquis Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made general of chariots and cavalry with headquarters opened and ceremonial honors equal to the three highest ministers, retaining his ranks as regular attendant, supervisor of the secretariat, and inspector; his posthumous title was Marquis Yi.

sentences.zh: 長子絢，字長素。

translations.literal: His eldest son Xuan, courtesy name Changsu.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son was Xuan, courtesy name Changsu.

sentences.zh: 年七歲，讀《論語》至「周監於二代」，外祖何尚之戲之曰：「耶耶乎文哉。」

translations.literal: At age seven, reading the Analects to "Zhou surveyed the two dynasties," his maternal grandfather He Shangzhi teased him, saying: "Grandfather, how literary!"
translations.idiomatic: At seven, reading the Analects to the line "Zhou surveyed the two dynasties," his maternal grandfather He Shangzhi joked, "Grandfather, how learned!"

sentences.zh: 絢即答曰：「草蓊風必偃。」

translations.literal: Xuan immediately replied: "When grass is lush, the wind must bend it.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan answered at once, "When the grass is thick, the wind must bend it."

sentences.zh: 少以敏惠見知。

translations.literal: In youth he was known for quick wit.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was known for sharp intelligence.

sentences.zh: 及長，篤志好學，官至秘書丞。

translations.literal: When grown, he devoted his will to loving learning and reached the office of secretary aide.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he devoted himself to study and rose to secretary aide.

sentences.zh: 年二十四，先景文卒，諡曰恭世子。

translations.literal: At twenty-four he died before Jingwen; posthumous title Filial Heir.
translations.idiomatic: He died at twenty-four, before Jingwen; his posthumous title was Filial Heir.

sentences.zh: 子婼襲封，齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: His son Ruo inherited the fief; when Qi received the mandate, the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ruo inherited the title; when Qi took the throne, the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 廢帝元徽初，復為黃門郎，東陽太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhui under Deposed Emperor, he again became palace gate gentleman and administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Yuanhui under Deposed Emperor, he again became a palace gate gentleman and administrator of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 未之郡，值桂陽王休範逼京邑，蘊領兵於朱雀門戰敗被創，事平，除侍中，出為寧朔將軍、湘州刺史。

translations.literal: Before reaching his commandery, when Prince Xiufan of Guiyang pressed the capital, Yun led troops at the Vermilion Bird Gate, was defeated and wounded; when order was restored he was made attendant-in-ordinary and sent out as general who calms the north and inspector of Xiang province.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached his post, Prince Guiyang Xiufan threatened the capital; Yun led troops at the Vermilion Bird Gate, was defeated and wounded; after order was restored he was made attendant-in-ordinary and sent out as general who calms the north and inspector of Xiang province.

sentences.zh: 蘊輕躁，薄於行業，時沈攸之為荊州刺史，密有異志，蘊與之結厚。

translations.literal: Yun was light and rash, thin in conduct; at the time Shen Youzhi was inspector of Jing province and secretly harbored disloyal intent—Yun bonded closely with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was impulsive and shallow in character; Shen Youzhi, then inspector of Jing province, secretly nursed rebellious designs, and Yun grew close to him.

sentences.zh: 及齊王輔朝政，蘊、攸之便連謀為亂，會遭母憂，還都，停巴陵十餘日，更與攸之成謀。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qi assisted court governance, Yun and Youzhi at once joined in plotting rebellion; meeting mourning for his mother, he returned to the capital, stopped at Baling more than ten days, and renewed conspiracy with Youzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince of Qi guided court affairs, Yun and Youzhi quickly plotted rebellion together; after his mother's death he returned to the capital, lingered at Baling more than ten days, and renewed his pact with Youzhi.

sentences.zh: 時齊王世子為郢州行事，蘊至郢州，謂世子必下慰之，欲因此為變，據夏口，與荊州連橫。

translations.literal: At that time the prince of Qi's heir apparent was acting for Ying province; Yun reached Ying province, thinking the heir would certainly come down to console him, wishing thereby to make a coup, hold Xiakou, and link horizontally with Jing province.
translations.idiomatic: The prince of Qi's heir was then acting governor of Ying province; Yun reached Ying, expecting the heir to come down and console him on his mourning, planning to seize the moment, hold Xiakou, and join forces with Jing province.

sentences.zh: 世子覺其意，稱疾不往，又嚴兵自衛，蘊計不得行，乃下。

translations.literal: The heir perceived his intent, pleaded illness and did not go, and also strictly armed himself for defense; Yun's plan could not proceed, and he went downriver.
translations.idiomatic: The heir saw through him, pleaded illness and stayed away, and tightened his guard; Yun's plot failed and he continued downstream.

sentences.zh: 及攸之為逆，蘊密與司徒袁粲等結謀，事在粲傳。

translations.literal: When Youzhi rebelled, Yun secretly joined in plotting with Minister of Works Yuan Can and others—the affair is in Can's biography.
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhi rose in rebellion, Yun secretly conspired with Minister of Works Yuan Can and others—the affair is recorded in Can's biography.

sentences.zh: 事敗，走鬬場，追禽，斬於秣陵市。

translations.literal: When the affair failed he fled to the drill ground, was pursued and captured, and beheaded in Moling market.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot failed he fled to the drill ground, was caught in pursuit, and beheaded in Moling market.

sentences.zh: 景文弟子孚，大明末，為海鹽令。

translations.literal: Jingwen's younger brother's son Fu, at the end of Daming, was magistrate of Haiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen's nephew Fu, in the late Daming era, served as magistrate of Haiyan.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，天下反叛，唯孚獨不同逆，官至司徒記室參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi the realm rebelled; only Fu alone did not join the rebellion, and reached the office of recording secretary on the minister of works' staff.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Taishi the empire rose in rebellion; Fu alone refused to join and rose to recording secretary under the minister of works.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：王景文弱年立譽，聲芳籍甚，榮貴之來，匪由勢至。

translations.literal: The historian says: Wang Jingwen won reputation in youth; his fame fragrant and weighty in the registers; the coming of glory and nobility was not from power's arrival.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Wang Jingwen won fame in youth, his reputation shining in the records; his rise to honor came not from brute power.

sentences.zh: 若泰始之朝，身非外戚，與袁粲群公方驂並路，傾覆之災，庶幾可免。

translations.literal: Had it been the court of Taishi and he not been maternal kin, with Yuan Can and the lords side by side on the road, the disaster of overturn might nearly have been avoided.
translations.idiomatic: Had he served in Taishi's court without being imperial kin, walking beside Yuan Can and the other lords, he might nearly have escaped ruin.

sentences.zh: 庾元規之讓中書令，義在此乎！

translations.literal: Was Yu Yuan's yielding the directorate of the Secretariat not righteous in this same sense!
translations.idiomatic: Was not Yu Yuan's refusal of the directorate of the secretariat righteous in just this sense?
